questions.stem: In an endothermic reaction, energy is transferred from:

options.text: The surroundings to the reaction system
The reaction system to the surroundings

questions.explanation: In an endothermic reaction, energy is absorbed from the surroundings into the reaction system. This causes the temperature of the surroundings to decrease, which is why endothermic reactions feel cold.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an endothermic process?

options.text: Citric acid reacting with sodium hydrogencarbonate

questions.explanation: The reaction between citric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate (baking soda) is a classic endothermic reaction. The mixture absorbs heat from the surroundings and the temperature drops noticeably. The other options are all exothermic.

questions.stem: On an energy level diagram for an endothermic reaction, what is the relative position of products and reactants?

options.text: Products are at a lower energy level than reactants
Products are at a higher energy level than reactants
Products and reactants are at the same energy level
Only the reactants are shown on the diagram

questions.explanation: In an endothermic reaction, the products have more energy than the reactants because energy has been absorbed from the surroundings. The products line is drawn higher than the reactants line on the energy level diagram.

questions.stem: What is the sign of ΔH for an endothermic reaction?
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions have a positive enthalpy change (ΔH > 0) because the system gains energy from the surroundings. The products contain more energy than the reactants.

questions.stem: Thermal decomposition requires continuous heating to proceed. What does this tell you about the reaction?

options.text: It is endothermic, as it needs a constant input of energy
It is neither exothermic nor endothermic
It is a reversible reaction only

questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition is endothermic because it requires continuous energy input (heating) to break down the compound. If you stop heating, the reaction stops, showing that energy must constantly be supplied.

questions.stem: Which practical application makes use of an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Instant cold packs for treating injuries

questions.explanation: Instant cold packs contain chemicals (often ammonium nitrate and water) that undergo an endothermic reaction when mixed. They absorb heat from the surroundings (the injured area), providing a cooling effect.

questions.stem: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction. Where does the energy input come from?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs light energy from the Sun to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. Without this energy input from sunlight, the endothermic reaction of photosynthesis cannot occur.
